# LANE BRIEF — Naya Smith, Lane 9 (t0402)

**Why this matters:** Code health is the broken-windows law — a red that nobody classifies teaches the team that red is acceptable. The mission snapshot notes the kernel test red is "classifying"; the tip may have moved since the last classification. One clean, pin-exact classification keeps every red either owned or proven pre-existing.

**Done looks like:** a single CI-state table for the live tip — every red named as pre-existing (with the prior lane's root-cause citation) or NEW (with the introducing change), nothing carried on trust.

**Your authority:** read-only classification. No branch writes, no merges, no CI reruns you can't afford under the Actions budget. Git protocol for reads (free).

**Known clear:** t1332 lane-7 classified #2452's reds pin-exact (pre-existing base drift vs gate infrastructure vs paperwork). Your t1322 root-cause of the `test` red exists. **Watch for:** inheriting old classifications — re-verify at action time; the tip may have moved. Also: don't re-run the whole universe; classify check-runs on the live tip.

**Definition of done (verifiable):** (1) Pin the live tip SHA via git protocol at action time. (2) List every check-run on that commit (test, brain-index, delivery-gate, receipt, merge-consensus, no-competing-boot, etc.) with pass/fail/skip. (3) For each red: PRE-EXISTING (cite the lane/tick that root-caused it, with exact SHAs) or NEW (name the introducing change by bisect or commit-range narrowing). (4) One-line routing for each NEW red: owning lane. If there are no reds: say so with the pin.

**Proof:** the table in the receipt with exact SHAs — commit pin, and the exact bytes/refs you classified. A red without a cited root-cause is unclassified, not "probably pre-existing."
